children: Lockheed Martin
secured more than
$1 billion in additional
U.S. Navy and Japanese defense contract awards

, extending its involvement in advanced fighter-jet systems and maritime missile defense. The agreements reinforce the defense contractor's long-term revenue visibility as military customers continue investing in aircraft modernization and sophisticated air-defense capabilities.

Lockheed Martin is one of the world's largest defense contractors, manufacturing F-35 fighter jets, missile-defense systems, military helicopters and advanced aerospace technology. It generates revenue primarily through long-term government contracts, with the U.S. Department of Defense representing its largest customer.
The latest awards include a
$244.96 million U.S. Navy contract modification
for additional F/A-18E/F Infrared Search and Track Block II systems.
The order covers 48 infrared receivers, including 45 for the Navy and three for the Royal Australian Air Force, alongside 74 processors, 27 inertial measurement units and supporting equipment.
Work is expected to continue through February 2031.
Separately, Lockheed secured a
$52.11 million modification
supporting engineering upgrades and additional capabilities for F-35 Lots 18 and 19, covering U.S. military branches, international partners and foreign military sales customers.
The largest award, however, involves Japan.
Lockheed's Rotary and Mission Systems division received a
$724 million contract modification
for Aegis combat systems aboard Japan's first two Aegis System-equipped vessels.
The modification raises the existing contract's total value from $1.64 billion to approximately
$2.36 billion
, with work scheduled through March 2030.
Investors Takeaway
The combined $1.02 billion in incremental awards strengthens Lockheed's contracted work pipeline, although the modifications should not be confused with entirely new standalone contracts.
Investors should monitor execution milestones, contract profitability and whether additional Japanese missile-defense spending translates into follow-on orders.

The extended delivery schedules also matter. Revenue recognition will occur over multiple years rather than immediately, making production efficiency, supply-chain stability and program margins important indicators of how effectively these awards contribute to future earnings.

title: Lockheed Martin Secures Over $1 Billion in Defense Deals
